summary: Module 1 full test. Backend: 17 pytest cases (health, config, dashboard stats, SIWE nonce/verify, replay, mismatch, wrong chain, bad signature, user lookup) all PASS via public URL. Frontend (390px): dashboard values, pool cards, activated/total users, bottom nav placeholders all correct. CRITICAL frontend blocker: the Connect Wallet bottom-sheet renders BELOW the fixed BottomNav (stacking-context bug) so 'Demo Wallet' (connect-demo-btn) cannot be clicked by a real user; normal click and force click both intercepted by nav subtree. Injecting the click via JS proved the SIWE flow itself works end-to-end (nonce -> verify -> UID TTN100011, Inactive badge, localStorage persistence, user re-fetch after reload).

minor.issue: Nonce is keyed per-address only (single doc, upsert). Requesting a new nonce silently invalidates any in-flight one; acceptable for Module 1 but note for multi-tab/multi-device.

ui_bugs.issue: WalletModal is rendered inside Header, which sits in App.js's `div.relative z-10` stacking context. The modal's z-[100] is therefore scoped inside z-10, while BottomNav (z-50) lives in the root stacking context — so the nav paints over the modal. Result: the bottom ~80px of the sheet (the Demo Wallet option) is covered and unclickable; Playwright reports 'nav[data-testid=bottom-nav] subtree intercepts pointer events'. Fix: render WalletModal via a portal to document.body (or move it out of the z-10 wrapper) and/or give the sheet bottom padding >= nav height.
After a successful connect, the sheet was still visible in the screenshot (onClose race / animation) — verify it always closes on success.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of the unclickable Demo Wallet button: CSS stacking contexts. WalletModal is a child of Header which is inside `<div class="relative z-10">` in App.js. A positioned element with z-index creates a stacking context, so the modal's z-[100] is only relative to that z-10 layer. BottomNav (fixed, z-50, backdrop-blur) is a sibling of that wrapper in the root stacking context and therefore paints above the entire modal, intercepting pointer events over the bottom 80px where the demo option sits.
